ImageDescription.value:
Westwood Village is the main shopping and commercial center of the Westwood district in the City of Los Angeles, California. It is located north of Wilshire Boulevard, east of Gayley Avenue, south of Le Conte Avenue, and west of Hilgard Avenue.

Opening in 1929, the original design was considered one of the most well planned and beautifully laid out of commercial areas in the nation. Harold Janss had hired major architects and instructed them to follow a Mediterranean theme, with clay tile roofs, decorative Spanish tile, paseos, patios and courtyards. Buildings located at strategic points, including theaters, used towers to serve as beacons for drivers on Wilshire Boulevard.

There is a link there to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0, which explains the meaning thereof. The base map is credited to http://www.openstreetmap.org/

The Times spells all this out at http://projects.latimes.com/mapping-la/about/#the-data
